description: Install a plugin from a local source directory at runtime and bring its entry-point online without restarting the homunculus. The verb validates the path exists, is a directory, and contains either plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml (refuses otherwise), runs `pip install -e <path>` against the active Python interpreter via subprocess, re-runs entry-point discovery on the plugin manager, and diffs the roster before and after to identify the newly installed plugin. On a successful install, the new plugin's process keys are collected from its get_available_actions and pushed into the registry via knowledge_service::refresh_plugin_processes so they become immediately invocable. The verb returns installed=true only when a brand-new plugin entry-point appears after install; an upgrade-in-place of an already-loaded plugin returns installed=false with an explanatory message and the caller should restart via apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin to swap in the new code. The pip subprocess inherits the active venv automatically (sys.executable -m pip). Refuses with a structured error if pip exits non-zero, surfacing the captured stderr so the caller can diagnose dependency conflicts.
embedding_description: Install a plugin from a local path at runtime. pip install -e a plugin source directory. Bring a freshly-checked-out plugin online without restarting the homunculus. Add a new plugin entry-point to the live orchestrator. Install a sibling plugin from a workbench scratch directory. Hot install a Python package as a homunculus plugin and register its process keys.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Install result with keys: installed (bool, true when a brand-new plugin entry-point appeared after install), plugin_name (str, name of the newly installed plugin or empty if none new), new_process_keys (list[str] of process keys the new plugin contributes), message (str status detail).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: On a successful install, confirm the plugin name and surface the new_process_keys count. If installed=false (upgrade-in-place of an already-loaded plugin), say so explicitly and recommend restart via apply_manifest to pick up the new code. If pip failed, surface the captured stderr verbatim so the caller can read the dependency conflict or build error.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: On installed=true, the new plugin's process keys are immediately invocable; the next step can call them. On installed=false, do not retry install — restart via apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin so the already-loaded plugin picks up the new bytecode. If the install succeeded but the plugin did not appear in the roster, check the package's pyproject.toml for an [project.entry-points."ananta.plugins"] block.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Install a plugin from a local directory via pip install -e and bring its entry-point online
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValidationError: path was empty, did not exist, was not a directory, or contained neither plugin.yaml nor pyproject.toml. PluginManagerUnavailable: the orchestrator's plugin_manager attribute is missing. PipInstallFailure: the pip subprocess exited non-zero — the captured stderr is in the error message; common causes are dependency conflicts, build errors, or a malformed pyproject.toml. NoNewEntryPointError: pip succeeded but no new plugin entry-point appeared on the plugin manager — the package may be an upgrade-in-place or may lack the ananta.plugins entry-point declaration.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For path errors: ensure the directory exists and contains plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml. For PipInstallFailure: read the stderr and resolve the underlying pip error before retrying; if the build needs system dependencies, install them first. For NoNewEntryPointError: if the goal is to refresh an already-installed plugin, restart via apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin; otherwise add the [project.entry-points."ananta.plugins"] block to the package's pyproject.toml and retry.
